data.narrative:
Space Forge, a Series G space and aerospace company co-founded by Joshua Western and Andrew Bacon, has raised $22.6M to date. The valuation exercise draws on a comparison universe of 5 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private-stage companies including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs—though narrow stage-specific comparables remain limited.

Of three potential valuation methods, only stage-progression proved applicable. Using $9M as a proxy for total capital deployed, and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical for Series G advancement, this method yields $11.25M. Peer-median analysis was not executable: while 14 same-sector peers exist, insufficient clustering at the same or adjacent stage precluded reliable median calculation. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (sector median: 25.3x across six tickers) could not be applied absent the target's revenue disclosure, standard practice for private companies.

The triangulation, constrained to a single method, supports a valuation range of $10M to $13M, with $11M as the median point. This range reflects modest step-up progression from total raised. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue data and sparse comparable transactions at Series G in frontier aerospace, limiting conviction in the multiple applied. Additional disclosure of revenue or ARR would substantially improve precision.
